claims.text: Formation and persistence of a protective oxide above 900 °C are governed by whether the oxide/metal interface reaches a critical density of misfit dislocations.
Si substitution reduces lattice mismatch at the oxide/metal interface.
Si substitution forms a Si-rich oxide that is crystallographically more compatible with the CrFeCoNi-based substrate.
A high density of interfacial misfit dislocations relaxes stress.
Stress relaxation by misfit dislocations prevents oxide-scale crack initiation and spallation.
A misfit-dislocation density below the critical threshold causes residual thermal-stress accumulation, oxide cracking, and spallation.
The relevant CrFeCoNiX alloys may be in single- or multiphase metallic solid-solution states.
The identity and amount of X modulate the lattice parameter of the metallic alloy.
The identity and amount of X modulate the lattice parameter of the oxide that forms.
Lattice mismatch between metallic and oxide phases can generate a high concentration of interfacial crystal defects or dislocations.
Metallic and oxide phases can retain the same crystal orientation despite substantial lattice mismatch and dense dislocations.
Sufficiently low lattice mismatch permits formation of a high density of misfit dislocations.
Dislocation-mediated stress relief fosters a coherent and adherent oxide scale.
Dislocation-mediated stress relief causes the oxide scale to grow slowly.
Alloys above the critical dislocation-density threshold will exhibit coherent, adherent, slow-growing scales with minimal cracking.
Alloys below the critical dislocation-density threshold will exhibit localized strain accumulation followed by cracking and spallation.
A minimally modified CrFeCoNi baseline will have poorer dislocation accommodation and a less stable oxide scale than suitably modified CrFeCoNiX alloys.
Temperature and oxygen partial pressure are relevant variables for high-temperature oxidation of CrMnFeCoNi.
The proposed threshold mechanism applies above 900 °C across Si-, Mn-, and Al-containing CrFeCoNiX alloys in single- or multiphase solid-solution states.
